chunks: He said: Abu 'Ali al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Fadhl al-Razi reported to me from Abul Hasan 'Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Bishr al-Askari, who reported from Abu Ishaq Muhammad ibn Harun ibn Isa al-Hashimi, who reported from Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Mahdi al-Ubulli, who reported from Ishaq ibn Sulayman al-Hashimi, who reported from his father, who reported from Harun al-Rashid, who reported from his father al-Mahdi, who reported from al-Mansur Abu Ja'far Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father, from his grandfather Ali ibn Abdillah ibn al-Abbas, from Abdullah ibn al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his progeny, saying:
"O people! On the Day of Resurrection we shall be four riders and none other." Someone asked: "May my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah! Who are the riders?"

He said: "I will be riding al-Buraq, and my brother Salih will be mounting the she-camel of Allah which was hamstrung by his people, and my daughter Fatimah will be on my she-camel al-Adba, and Ali ibn Abi Talib will ride a she-camel from the she-camels of Paradise whose bridle is of fresh pearls, whose eyes are of two red rubies, and whose belly is of green aquamarine. Upon it will be a dome of white pearl, translucent so that its exterior is visible from its interior and its interior from its exterior. Its exterior is from the mercy of Allah and its interior from the pardon of Allah. When it advances it hurries, and when it retreats it hurries."

And he will be ahead of me. Upon his head will be a crown of light, illuminating all the assembled. That crown has seventy corners, each corner shining like a brilliant star on the horizon of the sky. In his hand will be the Standard of Praise, and he will proclaim on the Day of Resurrection: "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah."

He will not pass by a group of angels except that they say: "A sent prophet!" And he will not pass by a sent prophet except that he says: "An angel near to Allah!" Then a caller will call out from the interior of the Throne: "O people! This is neither an angel near to Allah, nor a sent prophet, nor a carrier of the Throne. This is Ali ibn Abi Talib!"

Then his followers will come after him, and a caller will call out to his followers: "Who are you?" They will say: "We are the Alawiyyun." The call will come: "O Alawiyyun! You are secure. Enter Paradise with those whom you used to love."

key_terms.البراق: Al-Buraq: the celestial mount on which the Prophet traveled during the Night Journey (Isra and Mi'raj)
key_terms.العضباء: Al-Adba: the name of the Prophet's she-camel
key_terms.العلويون: Al-Alawiyyun: the partisans/followers of Ali ibn Abi Talib
key_terms.بطنان العرش: Butnan al-Arsh: the interior/depths of the Divine Throne
key_terms.لواء الحمد: Liwa al-Hamd: the Standard/Banner of Praise, carried on the Day of Judgment

ai.seo_question: Who are the four riders on the Day of Resurrection according to Islamic hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the Abbasid caliphal family chain, describes the Prophet Muhammad's teaching about four riders on the Day of Resurrection: himself on al-Buraq, Prophet Salih on Allah's she-camel, Fatimah on al-Adba, and Ali ibn Abi Talib on a jeweled she-camel of Paradise. Ali is depicted carrying the Standard of Praise and wearing a crown of light so magnificent that angels mistake him for a prophet and prophets mistake him for an angel. The hadith concludes with the promise that Ali's followers will enter Paradise with him.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 3. He said: Abu ‘Ali al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Fadhl al-Razi reported to me from Abul Hasan ‘Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Bishr al-Askari, who reported from Abu Ishaq Muhammad ibn Haroon ibn Isa al-Hashimi, who reported from Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Mahdi al-Ibili, who reported from Ishaq ibn Sulaiman al-Hashimi, who reported from his father, who reported from Haroon al-Rashid, who reported from his father al-Mahdi, who reported from al-Mansur Abu Ja’far Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Ali, from his father, from his grandfather ‘Ali ibn Abdillah ibn al-Abbas, from Abdillah ibn Abbas ibn Abdul Muttalib, who said: I heard the Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny say:
"Four of us will be the riders on the Day of Resurrection and none other." So someone asked: "My father and mother be your ransom, who are the riders?"

He said: "I will be riding al-Buraq, and my brother Swaleh will be mounting the god-sent she-camel which was hamstrung by his people, and my daughter Fatimah will be on my bright she-camel, and ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, who will ride one of the she-camels of Paradise, whose bridle will be of fresh pearls, whose eyes will of ruby, whose stomach will of green aquamarine; upon the camel will be cupola of translucent pearls, so that its exterior will be visible from within, and her interior will be seen from outside. Its exterior will be from the mercy of Allah, and its interior will be from His grace. She will be fast as she advances, and also as she retracts.

He will be ahead of me. There will be a crown of light on his head, a crown which will give light to all assembled. It will have seventy corners, each shining like a brilliant star in the heaven; and in his hands will be the praised standard, and he will set forth announcing: ’There is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is His messenger.’

And he will pass among the angels, they will say: ’He must be from the sent Prophets.’ And as he will pass by the Prophets, they will say: ’He must be an angel nearest to Allah.’ And then it will be announced from inside the Throne: ’O people! He is neither an angel nearest to Allah, nor a sent Prophet, nor a carrier of the Throne. He is ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib.’

Then his Shi’ahs will follow, and it will be announced: ’Who are you?’ They will say: ’We are the partisans of ‘Ali.’ The answer will come: ’O partisans of ‘Ali, you are secure; enter the Paradise and be with those who you loved."
